title: Working with Jabbo Smith at the Wisconsin Roof
summary: Levy worked with Jabbo Smith at the Wisconsin Roof in Milwaukee and admired his talent, though Jabbo drank.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. And... You know, did I tell you I worked with Jabba at the Wisconsin Roof? Yes. I thought Jabba was a real fine trumpeter.
How long were you at the Wisconsin Roof?
Oh, I think probably part of the... Well, at that time, I think they were only running a few nights a week.

Milwaukee, yes. Uh-huh. Wisconsin Roof, they called it, didn't they? About the years, got a theater. Yeah. And Jabba, I thought Jabba, I don't know why he didn't get further than he did. In fact, he had a lot of talent and...
He got to be a drinker.

Is that... Yeah, he got drank too much because he wrote a couple numbers and I raised them for him. And we were at the house and... And I didn't know he had that much talent. And he played them on the horn and I think I missed a note or something. And he... And he handled his voice. And he told me this was a note I had missed. And I didn't know the guy had the most talents because I didn't think he could read too fast, you know. But he was surprisingly much better than I thought he was. And then after I went and worked with him on Wisconsin Roof, why, I had a great admiration for him.
